source.quote: And man, the immediate vibes, the music, what a place to remember. The zone itself, there's beasts everywhere. All kinds, we got gorillas, panthers, tigers, you name it, it's probably here. But that makes sense because it's home to the original Hemet Nesingwary quest line. But beyond that, there's goblins, trolls, kurzen, humanoids, ogres, and much more. And this zone is absolutely packed with farming potential. So I think Goldie has his work cut out for him. And we better get started. Now, the first farm I want to go over is one that I have done before, long ago, and I figured we may may well see what kind of gold per hour it can provide now. So, still in northern Stranglethorn here, to the east of the Savage Coast, is a small island. And this island is home to a group of lesser water elementals. And luckily for us, these guys are on a forced spawn, so we can run laps around the island, repeatedly take them out, and never really have to worry about respawn timers. So, what do they drop, and what can we farm? Well, there's a few things on their actual loot table, and they're all water-based items. First up is enchanted water, which really isn't worth much. And then elemental water at around a 5% drop chance is like one gold each, and a similar rate for globes of waters, although a lower drop chance for those guys. But what we really want from these elementals, as far as trade goods go, are essence of waters. And these are a green trade good with a market value between 75 gold and 100 gold, depending on the day. So, we have ourselves another classic essence farm. And while we're farming away here, it is worth noting that Stranglethorn Vale also has some very big zone-wide drops. Pretty much every mob in both northern and southern Stranglethorn has a chance to drop a few rare items. So, every farm, including this elemental island farm, carries a serious lottery potential. First up is the Hyacinth Macaw, a parrot pet with a pretty wild market value north of 100,000 gold and a region sale average, which is pretty strong at 47.5k.

source.quote: Well, no zone drops this time, but I did get a Cavalier two-hander worth somewhere between 80 and 700 gold with a pretty decent like classic appearance. I also picked up the Moccasins of the White Hair, a blue BoE drop with a market value around 7,000 gold, although the average sale prices do sit closer to 500 gold, but still not bad for a little transmog on top of trade goods. And for the trade goods, it's 51 Elemental Water, not massive gold, 32 Essence of Water worth about 2,250 gold right now, 40 Globes of Water, and about 112 gold in vendor trash. So, all in, that brings the total trade good value for 1 hour farming here to roughly 2,480 gold per hour, which, honestly, not terrible, but it's definitely not going to get us a token very fast. But I do want to say, if you want to try this farm out, it would really shine in a five-man group where you could truly hyper spawn the elementals and dramatically increase your Essence of Water rates. And our next spot, because this zone is just so dense with farms, is only up the coast a little bit at the Ruins of Zul'Kunda. Up here, we do have the Bloodscalp trolls. So, they do have mystics, hunters, beast masters, and scouts roaming around the ruins, but the specific target here is the Bloodscalp mystic. That said, all of these mobs do share spawn points, and the ruins are pretty big and quite populated. And honestly, this is a familiar zone with classic players maybe meeting their untimely demises with how crowded these mobs are. So, let me know in the comments if you've had a run-in with these bad boys either back in the day or in hardcore. But in retail here, they do all share juicy Stranglethorn wide zone drops. I'll just be taking everything and clearing aggressively to try and force more mystics to respawn.
